Q: Are handler methods technically optional in a Razor Pages PageModel? A:

Yes, GET requests render the razor page by default. Also yes, the .cshtml file is mandatory, because the framework uses it for routing, but it only strictly needs the @page directive.

You could even add Layout = null; to suppress the rendering of _Layout.cshtml.

Personally I see no issue with having Razor Pages for APIs. Why deal with two routing systems? But “Minimal APIs” are also pretty easy if want to try them.

Q: How can I implement modulo (%) using only addition, multiplication, and comparison on the natural numbers (excluding 0)? A:

I used two loops:

The first one to search the highest natural such that Nmax x b < a.

The second, searchs for the highest natural modulo such that Nmax x b + modulo <= a.

As @furas mentioned, the case a == b results in 0, wich is excluded in your arithmetic. The case b > a results in modulo = a.

def __mod__(self, other):
    assert isinstance(other, Natural), "other must be a natural"
    a = self.val
    b = other.val
    if b > a:
        return self
    if b < a:
        nmax = 1 # maximum divisor
        n = 1
        
        while n * b < a:
            nmax = n
            n = n + 1
        
        product = nmax * b
        modulo = 1
        
        while product + modulo < a:
            modulo = modulo + 1
        
        return Natural(modulo)

Q: Can there be 2 different UTF-8 encodings for the same character? A:

(I'm answering your subject question, "Can there be 2 different UTF-8 encodings for the same character?", which is significantly different from the question inside the post.)

("Character" usually means string element. It's ambiguous at best, and it's not the right word to use here. The Unicode term for a visual representation, a glyph, is "grapheme".)

Yes, there are more than sequence of code points can result in the same grapheme. For example, both

U+00EB  LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH DIAERESIS

and

U+0065  LATIN SMALL LETTER E
U+0308  COMBINING DIAERESIS

should display as "ë". Let's see how your browser does:

  • U+00EB: "ë"
  • U+0065,0308: "ë"

In UTF-8, these code points would be encoded as

  • U+00EB: C3 AB
  • U+0065,0308: 65 CC 88

One would use Unicode::Normalize's NFC or NFD to normalize a string to one of two formats (your choice).

use feature qw( say );

use Unicode::Normalize;

my $x = "\x{00EB}";
my $y = "\x{0065}\x{0308}";

say      $x   eq      $y   ?1:0;
say NFC( $x ) eq NFC( $y ) ?1:0;
say NFD( $x ) eq NFD( $y ) ?1:0;

Output:

0
1
1

There's also something called "overlong" encodings in UTF-8. (Specifically UTF-8, not Unicode in general.) In UTF-8, Unicode code points are encoded using one of the four following bit patterns:

1 0xxxxxxx
2 110xxxxx 10xxxxxx
3 1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
4 11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx

The "x"s represent the code point to encode. One must use the shortest possible, so U+00EB would be

0000 0000 1110 1011
      --- ---- ----

   -----   ------
110xxxxx 10xxxxxx
11000011 10101011
C3       AB

But someone clever might do

0000 0000 1110 1011
---- ---- ---- ----

    ----   ------   ------
1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
11100000 10000011 10101011
E0       83       AB

Applications should reject E0 83 AB (or at least convert it to C3 AB). But some don't, and that can cause security problems. Perl's Encode module treats that sequence as invalid, so it shouldn't be an issue for Perl.

Q: Can't Get Curl Enabled in PHP 7.3.9 A:

The problem may arise because both Apache and PHP ship with some of the same DLLs, but different versions, perhaps notably nghttp2.dll.

The version provided with Apache will be loaded, since it is in the same directory as httpd.exe. But PHP's cURL extension may require a newer version.

This can occur with any combination of Apache and PHP versions where the PHP version is more recently released and a PHP extension requires a newer version of a DLL that Apache also provides. (I encountered it with Apache 2.4.41 and PHP 8.3.11.)

Solutions are either:

  • Update Apache;
  • Rename the DLL in the Apache bin folder so that the version provided with PHP is loaded instead.

More information and some discussion is at GitHub php-src issue #12491.

Q: Javascript DOM .querySelector() null issue A:

You could use querySelectorAll() and loop over the results. If there's no match, the loop will be empty.

document.querySelectorAll('.tab.active').forEach(el => el.classList.remove('active'));

This is essentially what the jQuery code does, since methods like removeClass() automatically operate on all the elements in the collection.

And like the jQuery methods, this allows you to use the same code whether you're operating on a single element or multiple.
